title: Build a Click Counter
prompt:
Elements `button` (a "increment" button) and `display` (shows the count) are provided as variables.

1. Add a click listener to `button` that increases `count` (starting at 0) and updates `display.textContent` with the new count.
2. To prove it works, simulate two clicks by CALLING the handler logic twice, then log `display.textContent` — it should print 2.

Tip: keep the handler in a variable or use a named function so you can call it yourself.

tests.name: a click listener is registered
two clicks lead to display showing 2
tests.hint: Count in the outer `count` variable; set display.textContent = count inside the handler; call the handler twice.

tests.name: the count was logged
tests.hint: console.log(display.textContent); after triggering the handler twice.
